title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-07-22
body:
Attendees: Ava, Ravi, Marta, Owen, Li (brief), + async from SRE

Sprint / context
- This is the weekly sync covering kernel optimizations, KV cache work, and batching improvements. Focusing on stabilizing the kernel changes that landed last Monday and rolling out KV cache memory reductions to Dedicated pools.

High-level summary
- Kernel changes (fused attention + matmul tiling) are delivering consistent p50 latency wins and higher throughput on long sequences. Still seeing a tail latency regression on rare GPT-style long-context requests when combined with dynamic batching — investigating.
- KV cache refactor into contiguous slab allocator merged to main for xlarge models; preliminary infra rollout on staging shows ~18% memory reduction for 8k+ sequences and reduced GC churn. Found one eviction bug that could OOM on sequences >64k tokens; hotfix in PR 1287.
- Batching: adaptive timeout experiments look promising (avg batch size up 12%, cost/token down ~7%), but p99 latency increased slightly under peak load; tuning required to balance SLOs.

Details: Kernel work
- What landed: fused QKV kernel (PR 1279) + matmul tiling heuristics (PR 1291). Both enabled behind feature flags; we enabled for Llama-3-13B and Falcon-40B on staging.
- Measured on A100-80GB and H100-80GB:
  - Llama-3-13B, seq_len=4096: p50 down 9–11%, throughput up 13% (tokens/sec).
  - Falcon-40B, seq_len=8192: p50 down 6–8%, throughput up 10%.
  - p99: mixed results — some requests (mixed sequence lengths + heavy plugin callbacks) saw p99 regressions of ~10–15% when feature flags enabled.
- Root cause hypothesis for p99: scheduling interactions between matmul tiling kernel and our existing inter-request preemption. The new kernels take longer single-threaded contiguous GPU time slices causing queuing of latency-sensitive requests.
- Next steps: add NVTX spans and per-kernel timing to traces (Marta), add a preemption heuristic to split long-kernel ops (Ravi), ramp kernel flag to 50% for staged traffic after heuristic.

Details: KV cache
- Change: refactor from per-request vector-of-buffers to shared contiguous slab allocator with per-request offsets. Improves locality and reduces malloc/free overhead.
- Results (staging Dedicated pool): average GPU memory used per 8k seq request down ~18%, cache hit latency improved ~6ms median.
- Bug found: under heavy long-history workloads eviction logic could compute wrong base offset leading to occasional OOB reads -> manifested as rare segfaults / OOM on long sequences (>64k). Root cause in offset wrap logic; hotfix applied in PR 1287 and backported to 2026-07-22 release branch.
- Rollout plan: ship hotfix to prod Dedicated cluster in a canary (5 hosts) tomorrow, monitor OOMs and cache-hit rates. If green after 24h, expand to 35% then 100%.

Details: Batching & scheduling
- Experiment: adaptive batching timeout that increases wait window when queue depth low and tightens when high. Intention is to get better batch fill without harming tail latency.
- Observed: average batch size +12% (good), cost/token -7% (good), but p99 latency up 12% during 2 short peak windows in the test run. Those peaks correlated with concurrent kernel-heavy model runs.
- Action: integrate batch timeout with model-specific kernel cost estimates so heavy-kernel models get stricter timeouts. Prototype by end of week (Owen).

Stability / incidents
- Incident on staging: two Dedicated hosts crashed yesterday due to the KV eviction bug; crash reconciles have been fixed and hotfix applied. No customer-facing incidents yet.
- Telemetry gaps: we still need per-kernel memory allocation traces to correlate allocation spikes with p99. Added as work item (Marta).

Performance numbers (staging A100 / typical runs)
- Llama-3-13B @ 4k: p50 9–11% lower, throughput +13%
- Falcon-40B @ 8k: p50 6–8% lower, throughput +10%
- KV memory: avg per-request memory -18% for 8k+ sequences
- Cost/token (combined changes): ~ -7% on test workloads

Blockers / risks
- Kernel preemption heuristic needs careful design — risk of perf regressions if splitting kernels naively.
- Eviction bug fixed but we need more long-history load tests to be confident.
- Batching tuning interacts with model-specific kernel costs; if we mis-tune, latency-sensitive apps could see regressions.

Work planned next week (owners)
- Add NVTX & per-kernel timing to traces (Marta) — due 2026-07-24.
- Implement kernel preemption heuristic and run microbenchmarks (Ravi) — prototype 2026-07-26.
- Rollout KV hotfix to 5 host canary and monitor (Ava) — start 2026-07-23.
- Integrate kernel-cost signals into adaptive batching timeout (Owen) — prototype 2026-07-25.
- Run long-history stress harness (Li) across Dedicated pools to validate eviction fix — run 48h starting 2026-07-23.

Open questions / discussion items
- How aggressive do we want kernel-level preemption? tradeoffs between throughput and p99.
- Should we add a per-customer latency-priority tag so routing/batching gives priority? (cost/complexity tradeoff)

Notes / quick links
- PRs: 1279 (fused-qkv), 1287 (kv-hotfix), 1291 (matmul-tiling).
- Jira: SERV-4523 (kernel perf), SERV-4571 (kv-eviction-oob).
- Next sync: Fri 2026-07-24 10:00 PT (short standup)

Triage / TODO (short)
- [Ava] kickoff canary rollout for kv-hotfix 7/23
- [Ravi] prototype kernel preemption 7/26
- [Marta] NVTX/per-kernel timing 7/24
- [Owen] batching + kernel-cost integration 7/25
- [Li] run long-history stress 7/23-7/25

Notes to self: keep an eye on SRE alerts for p99 increases during canary; coordinate with SRE to set temporary alert thresholds while kernel flags ramp.

-- end of update --
